questions.stem: Where can you see the runs of all pipelines, notebooks and dataflows you have access to, with their status and duration, in one place?

options.text: The workspace's Git panel
The Monitoring hub
The OneLake catalog
The capacity admin portal only

questions.explanation: The Monitoring hub lists activities across Fabric items you can access, with filters for status, item type and time.

questions.stem: You need to see only the ingestion jobs that failed in the last 24 hours across your workspaces. What do you do in the Monitor hub's job runs?

options.text: Set the time range to 24 hours and filter by status
Open each lakehouse's table properties for load errors
Read the Git history of each workspace
Run a deployment pipeline to compare the stages

questions.explanation: The job runs list filters by time range, item type, status and workspace, and supports keyword search.

questions.stem: Your team wants the logs of all a workspace's items in one place that they can query with KQL. What do you turn on?

options.text: Workspace monitoring
V-Order
High concurrency
Shortcut caching

questions.explanation: Workspace monitoring collects logs and metrics from the workspace's items into a monitoring eventhouse that you query with KQL.

questions.stem: Which two places tell you whether an eventstream is receiving and sending events? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: The eventstream's data insights, with incoming and outgoing event metrics
The lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint
The deployment pipeline's compare view
The workspace's Git panel
The eventstream's runtime logs

questions.explanation: Eventstreams show data insights (event counts and rates) and runtime logs for their sources and destinations.

questions.stem: You type part of a pipeline's name in the search box of the Monitor hub's Job runs page, but a run you know exists doesn't appear. The run is further down the list on a later page. What should you do instead?

options.text: Export the pipeline's JSON definition from the workspace and search the file for the missing run ID
Clear the browser cache so that the search box indexes every run in the workspace
Use the Item type, Status or Workspace filter drop-downs, which aren't limited to the loaded page
Turn on workspace monitoring, which makes keyword search cover the older pages of runs

questions.explanation: Keyword search only checks items loaded on the current page, while the filter drop-downs don't have this limitation. Workspace monitoring and the browser cache don't change how the search box works.

questions.stem: A Copy job was triggered a minute ago, but the Job runs page you opened earlier still doesn't show it. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The run is still waiting in a capacity queue, which the Job runs page never displays until the run starts
Runs appear only after they finish, so in-progress runs are hidden from the Job runs page
The page loaded its data when you opened it and doesn't update continuously, so you must select Reload
Copy jobs appear only in the capacity metrics app, not in the Monitor hub's Job runs page

questions.explanation: The Job runs page retrieves data when it loads and doesn't refresh on its own; the Reload icon shows new and active runs. Copy jobs are a supported item type, and in-progress runs are shown with an In progress status.

questions.stem: A team still ingests some data with a Dataflow Gen1. They can see their pipeline and Dataflow Gen2 runs on the Monitor hub's Job runs page, but never the Dataflow Gen1 runs. Why?

options.text: Dataflow Gen1 runs appear only after workspace monitoring is enabled
The Job runs page doesn't support or show Dataflow Gen1
The team needs the Admin role in the workspace to see dataflow runs
The Dataflow Gen1 runs are filtered out because the default time range is one hour

questions.explanation: The Job runs page lists many item types, including Dataflow Gen2, but explicitly doesn't support Dataflow Gen1. Changing the time range, roles or workspace monitoring doesn't add Gen1 runs to that page.

questions.stem: A nightly ingestion pipeline has many activities. You want to see the activities of one run laid out on a timeline to spot which one took the longest. What should you open from the Job runs page?

options.text: The Capacity Metrics app's Storage page for the pipeline's workspace
The workspace's lineage view, then the pipeline's downstream items
The item's Run history, then the run's Run details, viewed as a Gantt chart
The pipeline's Settings tab, then the Concurrency setting

questions.explanation: From Run history you can open a run's advanced Run details and view the activities as a table or a Gantt chart. Lineage, pipeline settings and storage pages don't show per-activity timing for a run.

questions.stem: You turned on data collection for workspace monitoring today. A colleague wants to query last week's Copy job activity logs in the monitoring database. What will they find?

options.text: No logs at all until someone refreshes the monitoring database manually at the end of each day
Last week's logs, because turning on collection backfills the activity of the previous 30 days by default
Last week's logs, but only for the Copy job runs that failed during that week
Only activity from after collection was turned on, because workspace monitoring doesn't backfill

questions.explanation: Workspace monitoring starts collecting only after you turn it on and doesn't backfill earlier activity. The 30 days is the default retention of collected data, not a backfill window.

questions.stem: Which two statements about the monitoring database used by workspace monitoring are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Only workspace Admins can run KQL queries against it
Monitoring data is retained for 30 days by default
Monitoring data is kept forever and can't be limited by a policy
The monitoring database is read-only
Users can delete individual log rows to remove sensitive entries

questions.explanation: The monitoring database is read-only and keeps data for 30 days by default (you can change data policies). Users with at least the Contributor role can query it, so querying isn't limited to Admins.
